extracted.intended_audience: suitably qualified early-career researchers (postdocs, junior professors, holders of temporary qualification professorships) applying for Emmy Noether Independent Junior Research Groups in AI methods
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and evaluation requirements for applying to the DFG Emmy Noether Programme specifically for independent junior research groups in the field of artificial intelligence methods. Covers eligibility, required proposal structure and length for draft and full proposals, review stages, and funding/administrative conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: Eligible research projects (AI methods broadly defined)
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects based on research questions addressing the development or enhancement of AI methods of any kind, as well as the formation of method theories and the analysis and review of AI methods, are eligible for funding. Eligibility also extends to projects in the field of AI methods for model formation, process development and modelling, performance evaluation or architecture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term AI methods is very broadly defined and encompasses, but is not limited to, the following topics: machine learning, logic and reasoning, data analytics and data mining, knowledge representation, knowledge-based systems, planning, uncertainty modelling, Bayesian methods, explainability, inference and mathematical/formal description as well as an analysis of the above topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility (career stage / positions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdoctoral researchers, junior professors with temporary contracts in the early stage of their research career and those with temporary “qualification professorships” are eligible to submit proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals can generally be submitted two to four years after completing a doctorate. In the context of this call, eligibility within the four-year eligibility period is given with the submission of the draft proposals. The childcare regulation that is currently in force until 1 July 2020 (see guidelines 50.02, section 2.1.4.) applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouraged applicants (timing after doctorate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who have completed their doctorates within the past two years are particularly encouraged to apply so that they can establish themselves in research at an early stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic qualification and evidence of preliminary work
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are expected to have an above average doctorate and provide evidence of significant preliminary work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary work should be evidenced in the form of ambitious publications in internationally respected publication outlets or appropriate relevant experience based on industrial research in one of the aforementioned areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectations for international research experience
rubrics_metrics.description: International research experience should be demonstrated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include research visits abroad, international research collaborations or an international working environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review process: two-stage procedure and use of standard Emmy Noether review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The review process consists of two stages. In both stages, the review process is based on the standard criteria applicable in the Emmy Noether Programme (see DFG form 10.210).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first stage is based on draft proposals of not more than five pages; if positively reviewed, applicants are invited to submit a full proposal and give an oral presentation. The second stage and the funding decision are based on the full proposal and the oral presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft proposal: length limit and required structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The draft proposal may not exceed five pages in length and must be structured as follows: State of the art and preliminary work; Objectives; Work programme incl. proposed research methods; Requested funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under '4. Requested funds', it is sufficient to provide estimates; quotes do not need to be provided in the draft proposal phase. Only requests for staff and equipment funding in excess of €10,000, which are planned for the subsequent full proposal, must be justified with reference to the work programme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft proposal appendices and permitted documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The draft proposal must include an academic curriculum vitae including a list of up to ten of the most important publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No other documents need to be included at the draft proposal stage. Note that compared to the structure used in form 53.05 ('Project Description – Emmy Noether Programme') for full proposals, certain items have been omitted and do not need to be addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full proposal: length and oral presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: If invited after a positive draft review, the applicant will be invited to draw up a full proposal consisting of 20 pages and give an oral presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The second stage of the review process and the subsequent decision regarding funding are based on the full proposal and the oral presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requested funds: justification requirements for full proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: In the draft phase estimates are sufficient and quotes are not required. For the full proposal, requests for staff and equipment funding in excess of €10,000 must be justified with reference to the work programme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission language, method and deadlines for draft and full proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft proposals are to be submitted in English via email to tanja.gemein@dfg.de by 19 February 2020. The envisaged deadline for submitting full proposals is 29 July 2020.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft submission via email; follow the stated deadlines. (Contact addresses and procedural contacts are provided for inquiries.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding duration and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding is granted for two three-year periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful applicants will lead an independent junior research group over a period of six years, with the opportunity to refine their research profile and improve international visibility, preparing them for eligibility for a professorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted programme modules
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants can submit proposals for the usual modules of the Emmy Noether Programme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless otherwise noted here, the instructions in 54.01 ('Proposal Preparation Instructions – Project Proposals') and guidelines 50.02 ('Guidelines for Emmy Noether Programme') apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic aim and expectations for project integration
rubrics_metrics.description: This call is part of a strategic DFG funding initiative in the field of AI intended to promote collaboration between method developers and domain researchers, and to create/integrate professorships at interfaces between AI methodology development and respective research fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful applicants in either of the two funding lines will be given opportunities to exchange ideas and network at events; funded projects are expected to present their results within this context. The DFG intends to establish synergies with other initiatives such as Alexander von Humboldt Professorships.
